title: Minimum Edges for Graph Dimension d
description: Studies the function minEdges(d) giving the minimum number of edges in a graph of dimension exactly d. Formalizes known values (d=1..5), proves structural results for small dimensions, and states open conjectures about monotonicity, quadratic growth, and complete graph optimality.

meta.author: Formalized in Lean 4 (Mathlib)
originalContributions: Axiomatization of the minEdges(d) function for graph dimension
Known values for d=1..5 including the d=4 surprise (K_{3,3} beats K₅)
Small-dimension completeness: for d≤3, K_{d+1} is optimal
Proof that d=4 is the first deviation from the complete graph pattern
Verification that d=5 returns to the complete graph pattern
Monotonicity, quadratic growth, and complete graph optimality conjectures
Linear lower bound from rigidity and quadratic upper bound from complete graphs

references.title: The dimension of the unit distance graph

meta.historicalContext: Erdős asked about the dimension of graphs as unit-distance graphs in Euclidean space. The minimum number of edges needed for a given dimension reveals surprising structure: K_{3,3} achieves dimension 4 with fewer edges than K₅.

sections.title: Graph Dimension
sections.summary: Defines unit distance embeddings and the graph dimension function.

sections.title: Minimum Edge Function
sections.summary: Axiomatizes minEdges(d) as the minimum edge count among graphs of dimension d.

sections.title: Structural Results
sections.summary: Proves K_{d+1} optimality for d≤3, the d=4 surprise, and d=5 matching.

sections.title: General Bounds
sections.summary: Linear lower bound d ≤ minEdges(d) and quadratic upper bound minEdges(d) ≤ C(d+1,2).

sections.title: Open Questions and Conjectures
sections.summary: States monotonicity, quadratic growth Θ(d²), and complete graph optimality conjectures.

overview.summary: Investigates the minimum number of edges needed for a graph to have unit-distance dimension exactly d. For small d, complete graphs K_{d+1} are optimal, but K_{3,3} achieves dimension 4 with 9 edges (vs 10 for K₅), making d=4 the only known exception.
overview.keyIdea: The function minEdges(d) captures the trade-off between edge count and geometric dimension. The d=4 case shows that bipartite graphs can sometimes achieve high dimension more efficiently than complete graphs.
prerequisites: Basic real number arithmetic and casting

conclusion.summary: We formalize the minEdges function for graph dimension, recording five known values and proving structural results about the small-dimension pattern. The d=4 case (K_{3,3} beats K₅) is formally verified as a strict inequality. Key open questions about general growth remain as conjectures.
openQuestions: Is K_{d+1} optimal for all d ≠ 4?
